messages:
maya: quick follow-up on the probe staleness observations. saw a NA->EU failover thrash this morning where probes were ~45s stale and routes kept flipping. attaching short dump. do we split soft constraint checks into the runtime (fast, conservative) and leave complex hard constraints to the policy compiler?
sam: thanks, saw the dump. rough idea: runtime does only latency/capacity heuristics and a conservative penalty; compiler/sidecar does full region/tier constraint checks async. means we might briefly route to suboptimal region but avoid oscillation.
liam: question: what's our tolerance for brief cross-region hedging? product asked for <200ms 99th for EU customers. if we misroute to NA for 10s that might violate SLOs.
maya: right — the observed flips lasted ~30–60s total because probes never caught up during a transient. the quick runtime check would avoid immediate hard cut if probe_age > x, instead use decay penalty.
emily: could we instead make probes adaptive: increase frequency on observed variance, lower elsewhere? that reduces average staleness without splitting logic. downside: probe storm risk at scale. :thinking_face:
nate: +1 to adaptive probes but scoped: only increase frequency per-tenant when their slice shows instability. global ramping is dangerous. also need backoff jitter.
sam: another angle: maintain a small decision buffer in runtime: require 2 consecutive decision windows (e.g., 5s each) before performing region-switch unless metric delta > threshold. slows failover but reduces thrash.
liam: that sounds promising. combine with probe_age check: if probe_age < 5s allow 1-window immediate switch for critical SLO tenants, else require 2. gives us tiered behavior.
maya: agree. operationally we need explicit knobs: probe_age_threshold, required_consecutive_windows, critical_tenant_allow_immediate boolean. also need telemetry: how often runtime deferred switching vs forced.
emily: on policy-engine side, splitting constraints still helps: keep matchers + complex budget calculations in compiler so runtime payload small (less CPU on routers). compiler publishes a concise decision blob (allowed_regions, soft_penalty_map).
sam: format idea for decision blob: {"allowed_regions": ["eu","na"], "soft_penalties": {"na": 0.2}, "version": "vX"} — tiny and fast to eval. runtime merges with live signals.
nate: ops-bot: recorded probe jitter spike at 1759998820->1759998860 across eu1 probes.
ops-bot: Incident note: automation created fallback route to na for tenant 'acme-inc' at 1759998832; rollup: 12 min, ~0.5% increased tail latency for eu users.
maya: thanks. next steps proposal: 1) implement tiered decision windows + probe_age check in runtime (canary on staging). 2) implement per-tenant adaptive probe ramp with strict backoff/jitter. 3) produce decision-blob spec and a compiler PR to emit soft_penalty_map. 4) add telemetry (deferred_switch_count, probe_age_hist, decision_blob_version).
liam: +1. need to surface these knobs in console (per-tenant) for fast toggles.
emily: will prototype decision-blob format and a small serializer. timeline: PR this week for spec, prototype next sprint.
sam: i'll take runtime windowing change. can we also add a small sim harness to replay the spike and validate no thrash?
maya: yes — sim harness essential. sam, coordinate with emily for blob format. nate, can you add the telemetry counters in ops side?
nate: on it. will also add alert if deferred_switch_count > 5% for more than 10m.
maya: OK. last note: let's keep default conservative to avoid user-visible regressions. can escalate per-customer via console flags. thanks all. :rocket:
